question: What happened to TikTok's ownership and US operations in 2025?
text:
TikTok briefly went dark in the U.S. in January 2025, then stayed online while ByteDance negotiated a deal to restructure its U.S. operations. **The deal was signed in December 2025, but it didn’t close until January 22, 2026.** ([tradingview.com](https://www.tradingview.com/news/reuters.com%2C2025%3Anewsml_L3N3V310A%3A0-tiktok-s-journey-from-global-sensation-to-trump-target/?utm_source=openai))

- **January:** On January 17, the Supreme Court upheld a 2024 law requiring ByteDance, TikTok’s China-based parent, to divest its U.S. operations or face a ban. TikTok shut off U.S. access late on January 18 and began restoring it on January 19 after President-elect Donald Trump promised to delay enforcement. Apple and Google didn’t restore the app to their U.S. stores until February 13. ([supremecourt.gov](https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/24pdf/604us1r07_k536.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- **January through September:** Trump repeatedly delayed enforcement while negotiations continued. On September 25, he signed an executive order approving the proposed ownership framework and giving the parties more time to complete the deal. ([whitehouse.gov](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/09/saving-tiktok-while-protecting-national-security/?_bhlid=fda91d7ec34c815cadd836818ff70a8233639d59&cst=&utm_source=openai))
- **December:** On December 18, TikTok and ByteDance signed binding agreements to form a majority American-owned joint venture. Oracle, Silver Lake, and Abu Dhabi-based MGX would each hold **15%**, while ByteDance would retain **19.9%**. The venture would oversee U.S. user data, recommendation-algorithm security, and content moderation. The deal covered TikTok’s U.S. operations, not the sale of TikTok globally. ([ksl.com](https://www.ksl.com/article/51421311/tiktok-signs-deal-to-sell-us-unit-to-american-investor-led-venture?utm_source=openai))
